question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=6y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the general solution to the system of ODEs above?

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}].$*

current_example.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-7x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-7y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Find the general solution to the system of ODEs above.

*Hint: ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/1491c6c2e24414b0c589d74d4eec1187d45452dbcc630b9c7ba1bab99235e922.svg) where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/b059ea05040648e97d08f5563b4da7eb6a40d5dc36e450475de49e765bbd1d83.svg)*
current_example.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/eb7163b9c72a6eaa2a1535a10f7f9d422438c45ef7fe6e085a087a05b7744203.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/b14e91caf25856541795de4d999eefcf15ab160b5cab72c0d43f48d7a9b3888c.svg) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/92f45abca8cfb18243b443b2b93f2b093869bf133acc973fdd9a4a9b0f0dee0f.svg)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},
$$

where $\Phi(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $\mathbf{c}$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix $\Phi_0(t)$ of the system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/bd17ad4ddbc233580566f89bf77ef9af938787c408b1ed5af40235dbef643227.svg)

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} & t{e}^{-7t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-7t} \\ {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t},\end{aligned}
$$

where $c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.$
